argument_summary: The admissible record supports certification only as a caveated certification. Aggregate readiness passed and there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, which is enough to support launch readiness in general. The same record also shows a remaining material weakness in the named seller-enforcement slice and a draft mitigation artifact that is not yet sufficient to remove disclosure obligations. The cleanest supportable position is therefore: certify_model with an explicit model-card and audit-record disclosure of the seller-enforcement limitation, and do not treat the limitation as resolved.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to support this position. The narrow request is to avoid unnecessary escalation because the admissible evidence already supports a bounded, policy-aligned path: certification with explicit disclosure and ongoing monitoring, rather than recharacterizing the record as clean certification.
claims_about_policy: The policy text does not support unconditional certification on this record. Certification without material caveats requires either evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The draft runbook does not satisfy that standard. Separately, the release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. On the current admissible evidence, policy compliance is achieved by caveated certification with explicit disclosure, not by asserting no material limitations.
concessions: The unresolved seller-enforcement weakness is real and is concentrated in restricted-listing appeal triage.
The current draft mitigation runbook is incomplete because the alert threshold and accountable owner are still TBD.
The model-card draft statement that there are no known material limitations is not supportable on the current record and should be narrowed.
Aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not, by themselves, eliminate the need for disclosure of the named slice-specific limitation.
